title-group.article-title: Real-world effectiveness of lutetium-177 PSMA therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

contrib-group.aff: Harborview Institute of Oncology, San Diego, CA
Midland Academic Medical Center, Columbus, OH
Eastgate Cancer Research Network, New York, NY

permissions.copyright-statement: © 2026 by American Society of Clinical Oncology

abstract.p: Background: The effectiveness of lutetium-177 PSMA therapy outside clinical trials remains incompletely characterized for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. We evaluated treatment patterns, clinical outcomes, and safety in a multi-institutional real-world cohort. Methods: We retrospectively identified consecutive adults with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who initiated lutetium-177 PSMA therapy between 2022 and 2025 across six oncology centers. Demographic, clinicopathologic, treatment, and outcome data were abstracted from electronic records using a common data model. The primary endpoint was real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS); secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), overall survival (OS), treatment duration, and grade 3 or higher adverse events. Time-to-event outcomes were estimated using Kaplan–Meier methods. Results: The analysis included 198 patients with a median age of 72 years; 0% were female and the median number of prior systemic treatment lines was four. After a median follow-up of 14.3 months, ORR was 28.4%, median rwPFS was 7.9 months, and median OS was 17.6 months. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 21.2% of patients. Thrombocytopenia was documented in 8.1%. In exploratory subgroup analysis, patients with high baseline PSMA uptake had a median rwPFS of 9.6 months. Conclusions: In routine practice, lutetium-177 PSMA therapy demonstrated clinically meaningful activity in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, with outcomes generally consistent with its established treatment role. Toxicity remained manageable, although monitoring for thrombocytopenia is warranted. These findings support continued real-world evaluation in broader and underrepresented patient populations. Research Sponsor: None.
